name: CA-51
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by about 10 points on the partisan baseline
Incumbent Sara Jacobs is running and holds a large fundraising edge
Prediction markets price Democratic win odds near 96%
No general-election polling or expert ratings available
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Jacobs: a D+10 district, incumbency, and a fundraising advantage of roughly $1.6 million raised against a little-known challenger, with markets pricing her near certain to win. With no polls to contradict that picture, the forecast stays at a roughly 21-point Democratic margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much tighter race or unexpected outside spending against Jacobs would be the first sign this is closer than the fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Sara Jacobs, the Democratic incumbent in this San Diego-area district, advanced to the general election against Republican Ricardo Cabrera. The seat sits in territory that favors Democrats by double digits, and Jacobs enters with the advantages of incumbency and a substantial fundraising lead, having raised about $1.6 million while facing no outside opposition spending.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and prediction markets, which price Jacobs near certain to win. The expected margin is roughly 21 points, consistent with a Safe Democratic rating, though uncertainty is somewhat elevated given the absence of direct polling.
